'''''Stuckenia pectinata''''' ([[Synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''Potamogeton pectinatus''), commonly called '''sago pondweed'''<ref>{{PLANTS |id=STPE15 |taxon=''Stuckenia pectinata'' |access-date=4 December 2015 }}</ref> or '''fennel pondweed''',<ref name=IUCN/> and sometimes called '''ribbon weed''', is a [[Cosmopolitan distribution|cosmopolitan]] water plant species that grows in fresh and brackish water on all continents except [[Antarctica]].

==Description==
''Stuckenia pectinata'' has long narrow linear leaves which are less than 2 mm wide; each is composed of two slender, parallel tubes.<ref name=illwildflowers>{{Illinois Wildflowers|wetland|plants|sago_pondwd|Sago Pondweed (''Stuckenia pectinata'')|access-date=12 June 2026|html=1}}</ref>  It is a fully submerged [[aquatic plant]] and does not have any floating or emerged leaves.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Stuckenia pectinata'' - Fennel Pondweed |url=https://www.flowersofindia.net/catalog/slides/Fennel%20Pondweed.html |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=www.flowersofindia.net}}</ref>

The main difference from other narrow-leaved pondweeds{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} is that the [[stipule]] joins the leaf base, when it is pulled the sheath and stipule comes away, similar to a grass sheath and [[ligule]]. The flowers are borne in solitary [[spike (botany)|spike]] inflorescences with several clusters of flowers, up to six with interruptions along the peduncle.<ref name=illwildflowers/>  The fruits are 3 to 5 mm long.<ref name=illwildflowers/>

The flowers are wind pollinated and the seeds float. [[Tuber]]s that are rich in starch are formed on the rhizomes. [[Reproduction]] can either be [[vegetative reproduction|vegetative]] with tubers and plant fragments or sexual with seeds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-28 |title=Plant Reproduction |url=https://letstalkscience.ca/educational-resources/backgrounders/plant-reproduction |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=Let's Talk Science |language=en}}</ref>

==Ecology==
The nutritious tubers are an important food source for waterfowl, including the [[canvasback]], which help [[biological dispersal|disperse]] the plant.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000377 |title=''Stuckenia pectinata'' in Flora of North America @ efloras.org |website=www.efloras.org |access-date=2017-02-01}}</ref>  [[Trumpeter swan]]s and [[northern pintail]]s feed mostly on the leaves and seeds of the plant.<ref name=illwildflowers/>{{rp|Bird Table}}

A variety of insect larvae, including those of the [[Curculionidae]] (weevils), [[Trichoptera]] (caddisflies) and [[Crambidae]] (types of moth) are associated with this plant.<ref name=illwildflowers/>

The plant can become a nuisance [[noxious weed|weed]] in waterways such as canals, because it is tolerant to [[eutrophication]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=O’Hare |first1=Matthew T. |last2=Baattrup-Pedersen |first2=Annette |last3=Baumgarte |first3=Inga |last4=Freeman |first4=Anna |last5=Gunn |first5=Iain D.
